title: Neuraxial / Deep Blocks on Anticoagulants (ASRA 5th ed)
sources: Kopp SL, Vandermeulen E, McBane RD, et al. Regional Anesthesia in the Patient Receiving Antithrombotic or Thrombolytic Therapy, 5th Edition. ASRA Pain Medicine, 2025
Critical Vector — Neuraxial Blocks & Blood Thinners (verified against the ASRA 5th ed)

changelog.change: Initial entry from the CV ASRA 5th-edition summary (stop/restart times verified against the published guideline).

summary: ASRA 5th-edition (2025) stop-before and restart-after times for neuraxial and DEEP plexus / deep peripheral blocks. Spinal hematoma is rare but catastrophic in a fixed closed space — ASRA stays deliberately antihemorrhagic: the goal is full hemostasis, not a convenient compromise.

body.text: Deep plexus and deep peripheral blocks (lumbar plexus, deep paravertebral, proximal sciatic) follow the SAME rules as neuraxial. Aspirin or NSAIDs alone → no restriction, proceed. Most DOAC-specific advice is grade 2C ('we suggest') — judgment still matters.

items: A drug LEVEL can clear a block on its own: DOAC < 30 ng/mL, or anti-Xa activity ≤ 0.1 IU/mL — acceptable regardless of time elapsed. PT and aPTT do NOT rule out a DOAC effect — wrong tests.
Reversal agents (andexanet, idarucizumab, PCC) are explicitly NOT for enabling a block in routine patients.

body.text: Dabigatran with CrCl < 30: avoid unless a level confirms < 30 ng/mL — renal function drives dabigatran timing more than any other DOAC. Restart low dose ~6 h post-procedure; restart high dose at ≥ 24 h (48-72 h after high-bleed-risk surgery). For high-dose DOAC, remove the catheter 24 h BEFORE the next dose, not after.

items: UFH IV: stop 4-6 h + confirm normal coags before the block; resume IV heparin no sooner than 1 h after needle placement.
UFH low-dose SC (5,000 U): 4-6 h or a normal aPTT. High-dose SC: 12 h (≤ 20,000 U/day) or 24 h (> 20,000 U/day) + normal aPTT.

LMWH low (prophylactic) dose: 12 h before. High (therapeutic) dose: 24 h before. Restart prophylaxis ≥ 4 h after catheter removal; therapeutic at 24 h (48-72 h after high-bleed surgery). CrCl < 30 → double the wait times.
On any heparin > 4 days → check platelets first (HIT risk rises with exposure duration).
Warfarin: stop ≥ 5 days with a normalised INR; remove the catheter once INR < 1.5.
Fondaparinux low dose (2.5 mg): 36-42 h (58 h if CrCl 30-50; avoid if < 30). High dose (5-10 mg): 70 h (younger) / 105 h (elderly).
Thrombolytics: avoid the needle for ≥ 48 h and confirm normal clotting including fibrinogen.
Herbal supplements (garlic, ginkgo, ginseng): no need to stop.

body.text: Numbers to remember: high-dose apixaban/rivaroxaban/edoxaban 72 h · high-dose dabigatran 72 h (120 h if CrCl 30-49) · any DOAC level < 30 ng/mL or anti-Xa ≤ 0.1 IU/mL clears the block · warfarin 5+ days & INR < 1.5 · UFH IV 4-6 h + normal coags · LMWH high dose 24 h · clopidogrel/ticagrelor/prasugrel 5-7 / 5 / 7-10 days.
